title: Behavior-flag phased retirement playbook and evaluator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Consolidated playbook to retire behavior flags that affect streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs. Includes a systematic evaluator (golden prompt suite + replay checks), telemetry probes, and rollback guardrails. Goal: reduce flag surface by 50% for v1.20 while preserving client compatibility and measurable quality regressions < 1% on production prompts.
acceptance_criteria: Defined retirement schedule with clear owner and communication timeline for each flag
Migration guide published and linked from SDK release notes for major client languages
Automated evaluator runs against golden prompt suite with pass/fail thresholds and signal classification
Regression delta on production traffic for streaming latency and completion correctness < 1%
Fallback paths validated: model-variant routing and behavior-preserving adapter exist for each retired flag
Canary rollout plan and rollback triggers documented and automated in Console
tasks: Inventory active behavior flags and map to affected APIs (streaming/tool-calls/structured-output)
Prioritize flags by customer usage, internal telemetry, and potential surface area change
Author migration guide per-flag: example client patches, recommended API calls, and server-side compatibility layer notes
Build evaluator: golden prompts, structured-output schema checks, replay harness for non-deterministic streams
Define telemetry probes and dashboards: user-facing errors, malformed tool invocations, structured-output schema drift
Coordinate with SDK owners for migration PRs and code samples
Design canary plan: % rollout schedule, monitoring checks, and automated rollback criteria
Run internal beta with 2 power customers and collect compatibility feedback
discussion: 2025-02-03: Kickoff with Eng (Runtime + API) and DX. Consensus: retire only flags that have at least one documented migration path.
2025-02-10: Runtime team suggested adapter layer to translate legacy streaming chunk format to new structured delta format. Trade-off: adds ~0.5ms per-chunk overhead but reduces customer breakage.
2025-02-18: PM notes that some flags are heavily used by two enterprise customers; propose extended grace period + dedicated migration support.
2025-02-27: Legal asked to review audit log implications for flag-based behavioral differences. ETA 2025-03-10.
2025-03-01: SDK lead (Sofia Kim) requested code-level examples for Java and Python; assigned to Marco Ruiz.
decisions: All streaming-related flag retirements will include a runtime translation adapter for the first canary wave to reduce client changes
Structured-output flags that alter schema will require golden prompt passes and explicit opt-in removal for customers during canary
Tool/function calling flag removals will have a compatibility shim that validates invocation shapes and emits deprecation telemetry before failing
Behavior flags with >0.5% production usage require stakeholder alignment and a documented customer migration SLA
review_feedback: 2025-02-20 - Eng review (Priya S.): Add schema-level validation steps for structured outputs; recommended JSON Schema examples.
2025-02-24 - DX review (Sofia K.): Request to include sample SDK patch for streaming client to support new delta framing; suggested example repo link.
2025-03-03 - Security (Luis M.): Ensure adapter logs do not leak PII; flagged for engineering to add sanitization filter.
qa_plan: Unit tests for adapter translation layer
Integration test harness that replays historical traffic capture against new runtime with adapters enabled
End-to-end tests for tool-call contract validation including edge cases (nested args, binary payloads)
Non-regression latency tests for streaming path under realistic concurrency
test_plan: Golden prompt sweep: run suite of 250 curated prompts and compare structured-output schema + semantic diffs
A/B replay test: run 48-hour traffic replay with 10% of requests routed through new behavior (compare error rates)
Canary instrumentation: collect token-level latency, first-byte latency for streams, tool invocation success rate
Chaos scenarios: kill adapter process and validate graceful fallback to legacy path
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Internal): adapters enabled for internal and CI traffic only
Phase 1 (Private Beta): enable for 5% of production traffic with extensive monitoring
Phase 2 (Gradual Ramp): 5% -> 25% -> 50% over two weeks if no regressions
Phase 3 (Removal): after 30 days stable at 50% and customer migrations complete, decommission flag and cleanup code paths
Rollback triggers: >0.5% increase in user-facing errors, >1% regression on golden-suite pass rate, or sustained latency increase >10%
notes: We will publish a customer-facing migration timeline and a per-flag FAQ. Templates live in Drive attachment folder.
Consider offering migration workshops for top-tier customers during Phase 1.
Follow-on work: automate SDK code mods in repository using codemods (post-retirement).
